headline: Nineteen amendments filed, eleven moved, zero adopted
teaser: Councilors filed 19 amendments to the Moda Center term sheet. Eleven reached a roll call on Aug 6 — and the same six councilors voted Nay on every single one. Four failed on 6–6 ties. The final vote comes Aug 12.
body:
The term sheet — $120M from the City toward a $573M renovation, plus roughly $275M in maintenance commitments over 20 years — reached council with 19 proposed amendments from five councilors: rent for the Blazers, a share of naming-rights revenue, a higher payment-in-lieu-of-taxes escalator, proof of private financing, and more (per [OPB](https://www.opb.org/article/2026/08/06/portland-oregon-moda-center-trail-blazers-basketball/) and KGW).

**What the official record shows.** Eleven amendments were moved on Aug 6 and every one failed. The Nay column was identical all eleven times: **Clark, Zimmerman, Smith, Pirtle-Guiney, Ryan, Dunphy**. Koyama Lane, Green, Avalos, and Kanal voted Aye all eleven times; Morillo missed that mark only on Novick's amendment. Novick was the swing — Nay on the five-vote amendments, Aye on his own and the four that died 6–6. Amendments needed 7 votes; Mayor Wilson, who may break ties, broke none. The other eight filed amendments (Avalos 2–5 and 9–12) were never moved — not voted down, simply never brought to the floor.

**What council members said.** Council President Dunphy — elected in 2024 with Working Families Party backing and counted by Rose City Reform among the council's six-member Progressive Caucus — announced before the votes that he and Pirtle-Guiney would vote down every amendment, favoring a clean continuation of negotiations (per OPB). The amendment sponsors saw it differently; see the quotes below.

**On the question of who said nothing:** the roll calls are the only primary-source record of Councilor Zimmerman's position — he voted Nay on all eleven motions, and none of the accessible coverage of the Aug 5–6 sessions quotes him or records him speaking during the amendment debate. Before the vote, he told KGW he was 'not too worried about the process' and has been generally more publicly supportive of spending public money on the renovation; KGW also noted he did not respond to their emails before publication. Whether he spoke on the dais on Aug 6 can be settled only by the meeting video — this note will be updated when that's checked.

**What's next:** the resolution returns **Aug 12, 2026, 9:30 a.m.** for final amendments and a final vote; passage needs 7 of 12. Dunphy has said he may bring a comprehensive amendment incorporating the four 6–6 proposals (per OPB).

quotes.speaker: morillo
quotes.text: I am literally begging you to take these amendments seriously moving forward… Why would we not do it right now while we have the opportunity? I genuinely do not understand.

quotes.speaker: avalos
quotes.text: The current term sheet is absolutely unacceptable.

quotes.speaker: kanal
quotes.text: The amendments were the council's only meaningful opportunity to shape negotiations.
